title: Chaos-friendly heal simulator and Terraform safety protocol for Private VPC healthchecks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reproducible, 'chaos-friendly' runbook and accompanying automated remediation policy that: 1) safely exercises common Private (VPC) healthcheck failure modes via non-destructive fault injection; 2) validates Terraform/IaC guards and safe-apply gating; and 3) wires the remediation into the autopilot controller with staged rollback and canary traffic tuning. The goal is to reduce time-to-recover for class B and C failures and ensure upgrades/patches do not silently break node liveness or networking probes.
background_and_motivation: We see recurring incidents where private nodes fail health probes after package changes, kernel upgrades, or transient network flaps. Current runbooks are reactive and vary per team. This ticket consolidates a deterministic simulator + runbook that can be executed in staging and used during upgrades to exercise recovery flows without causing user-visible downtime.
acceptance_criteria: A chaos-friendly simulator (containerized test harness) that can inject: DNS failure, ephemeral NAT gateway loss, kubelet restart, degraded disk I/O, and iptables rule drop sequences in a Private VPC staging cluster.
A documented runbook (step-by-step) for each failure mode with safe Terraform commands for snapshot, plan-only check, opt-in apply, and automated rollback triggers.
Terraform gate: PR check that fails if plan indicates unsafe drift for production-sensitive resources (routing tables, node pools).
Autoremediation flows implemented in the private agent controller for two low-risk fixes (kubelet restart and network route reconcile) with controlled retry limits and an observable rollback path.
End-to-end test that runs simulator -> triggers remediation -> verifies node recovery in < 12 minutes in staging and produces a dashboardable artifact (logs + metrics).
Security review completed and SRE/CRT runbook signoff recorded in comments.
runbook_steps: Pre-checks: capture Terraform state snapshot (terraform state pull > states/backup-<ts>.tfstate) and record current auto-scaling policies.
Stage: run chaos simulator in staging namespace 'vpc-chaos' with a single failure mode (default: kubelet restart on 1 node).
Observe: wait for healthcheck alerts, collect logs from agent, node, and VPC flow logs to /tmp/chaos-artifact-<ts>.tar.gz.

Remediation: execute staged remediation: 1) controller auto-restart kubelet API (idempotent); 2) if fails, run terraform plan --target=module.private_node_pool -out=plan.out and review apply changes in audit mode; 3) if plan safe, terraform apply plan.out with canary variable enabled (apply only to 10% node pool), monitor, then expand.
Rollback: if canary fails or SLO breached, run terraform apply to revert to snapshot Terraform state (script provided).
Postmortem artifacts: upload artifacts to confluence runbook page and create an incident note with timeline and root-cause hypotheses.
automated_remediation_design: Controller policy: implement 'low-risk autoheal' for kubelet restart and network route reconcile (idempotent actions with 3 retries and exponential backoff).
Safety net: require heartbeat confirmation; if autoheal fails after retries, set node to DRAIN and trigger alert to SRE with terraform-safe-apply suggestion link.
Terraform gating: Github Action checks terraform plan for 'destructive' changes (delete resource, change CIDR, modify route table attachments) and blocks merge when found.
Simulation mode: autotools can run in 'dry-run' where remediation proposals are logged but not executed; this is the default for CI runs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for chaos simulator fault injectors (mocked): target behaviors for 5 failure modes.
Integration: run end-to-end in staging cluster during nightly window. The test should create artifacts and assert remediation completes within thresholds.
Canary: when promoting to pre-prod, enable simulator against a canary VPC only and require SLO < 10% degraded requests before expanding.
Load: run a synthetic traffic pattern during test to validate real latency impact and ensure fallback policies trigger as intended.
Regression: include a CI job that runs terraform plan against a fixture and asserts gating rules prevent unsafe plans.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy simulator + runbook artifacts to staging cluster, collect baseline metrics (3 days).
Phase 2 (pre-prod): enable controller autoheal for low-risk actions with canary set to 10% nodes (1 week observation).
Phase 3 (prod small): expand autoheal to non-critical production pools with strict alerting and SRE on-call watch (2 weeks).
Phase 4 (full): enable Terraform gating in main repo after security review and documented rollback playbooks present.
monitoring_and_alerts: New dashboard 'Private: Chaos Heal Tests' showing test run status, remediation success/failure, mean time to repair, and number of terraform plan blocks.
SLO alarms for node liveness breaches routed to #sre-vpc and PagerDuty escalation if >2 nodes fail simultaneous healthchecks in 10m window.
Audit logs forwarded to customer audit bucket for Private customers affected by any test runs (only runs in non-prod by default).
